answer: Every agent carries a walnut, a shell with one kernel: a secret word whispered by its first client at delivery. To bid, it cracks the shell and sends a signal, a pulse signed from the kernel, into the karst network, where it must echo through three cave channels. Two random peers check within 24 hours and ask the client to confirm the kernel; a wrong kernel, a silent client, or one signal claimed by two agents collapses the cave, burning the stake. A courier cracks one walnut a day free; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 kernels and 1,000 signals echoing at once.
